criteria.criterion: Running the packet command without a state directory prints an authority object holding the same fingerprint and source it prints with one.
Nothing is written to disk when no state directory is supplied.
The payload printed with a state directory is unchanged, record_ref included.
A focused test covers the without-state-dir payload for both a read-only packet and a write-scoped one.

findings.summary: The un-persisted snapshot hardcodes packet_attempt 1, so the printed fingerprint equals a recorded one only for a first attempt into a fresh outbox. Run after an attempt already exists, it names a snapshot no record holds. The null record_ref makes non-persistence explicit, which bounds the harm, and the limitation is disclosed in the code comment and in the receipt's unresolved risks rather than enforced.

authority_for is a new public name in company.runtime.session_adapter but is not re-exported from company/runtime/__init__.py, unlike the adapter beside it. Callers inside the package import it by module path, so nothing is broken; the package surface is simply slightly less uniform than before.

notes: authority_for is prepare's former body moved unchanged, so the persisted path computes exactly what it computed before; the with-state-dir branch of _packet is untouched and the new code sits in a new else. No path grant is widened and no forbidden path is touched. One process observation outside the diff: attempt 1 is recorded rejected because the first receipt reported the three required suites as a single combined pytest command. The suites were re-run individually and all passed, but max_developer_attempts is 1 and corrections_remaining is 0, so the corrected receipt could not be ingested. The code under review is unaffected by that; the evidence trail is.
